title: The audit opinion - the line worth reading before any of the numbers
subtitle: Four kinds of opinion, and why three of them are a reason to stop
whyItMatters: The auditor read this set of accounts before you did and wrote a page saying how far they believe it. That page sits at the very front, takes under two minutes to read, and decides whether any of the analysis behind it means anything.
openingQuestion: The audit report states an "unqualified opinion". What does that guarantee?
openingOptions: The accounts give a true and fair view in all material respects
The business is financially healthy and trading profitably
Every figure in the accounts is exact to the last dong
There was no fraud during the period audited
explanation: An unqualified opinion speaks to the quality of the PRESENTATION, not to the health of the business: a company deep in losses and heading for insolvency can still receive one, provided it presents those losses truthfully. Auditing also works on materiality and sampling, so it does not guarantee every dong, and it is not a fraud investigation - detecting fraud is a secondary objective rather than the main one.

diagram.label: Unqualified: trustworthy, read on as normal
Qualified: trustworthy EXCEPT one named item
Adverse: does not give a true and fair view - stop
Disclaimer: no basis for an opinion at all - stop

realWorldExample.company: The "material uncertainty about going concern" paragraph
realWorldExample.description: This is not a kind of opinion but an emphasis paragraph that can accompany an unqualified one. It says the auditor believes the accounts are presented truthfully, and simultaneously believes the business may not survive the next twelve months. Skipping this paragraph means skipping the strongest warning a set of accounts can issue.

sections.text: Before analysing a single figure, there is a question cheaper than any calculation: what did the person who checked these accounts say about them? The answer is on the first page and takes under two minutes to read.
Four kinds of opinion, in order of severity

sections.title: Only the first lets you read on as normal
sections.subtitle: The other three all change how you must treat every figure that follows

concepts.def: The accounts give a true and fair view in all material respects. This is the ordinary outcome rather than a compliment - it speaks to presentation, not to the business trading well.
Trustworthy, EXCEPT one specifically named item. The rest remains usable, but the excepted item has to be reassessed yourself - and if it is large, much of your analysis rests on it.

The auditor concludes the accounts do NOT give a true and fair view. Very rare, because companies usually correct things before it reaches this point. When it appears, none of the figures can be used for analysis.
The auditor could not gather enough evidence to conclude anything. Usually because the scope of their work was restricted - and that restriction is itself information.

sections.text: A qualification is not a vague warning

A qualified opinion always names the item and the reason. For example: the auditor could not observe the opening inventory count because they were appointed after that date, so they cannot confirm inventory of 800 billion. That means everything derived from inventory - cost of sales, gross margin, turnover, profit - carries that same uncertainty. The thing to do is read the basis-for-qualification paragraph, see how large the item is against total assets, and then decide whether your analysis still stands.

sections.label: Three things an audit opinion does NOT guarantee
sections.text: It does not guarantee the business is healthy: a chronically loss-making company still receives an unqualified opinion if it presents those losses truthfully. It does not guarantee every figure is exact: auditing works on materiality and sampling, so small errors fall outside its scope. And it is not a fraud investigation: detecting fraud is a responsibility but not the main objective, and a fraud involving collusion by management can pass through entirely.

items: Read the audit opinion first - two minutes that decide all the analysis behind it
An unqualified opinion speaks to presentation, not to the business trading well
A qualification always names the item - find out how large it is
A going concern paragraph can accompany an unqualified opinion

lines: The audit opinion does not say whether the business is good or bad - it says whether this set of numbers is worth your effort.
Having read these three lessons, you now have the framework to return to the Apple and Vinamilk cases with a different eye.

quiz.question: What does an unqualified opinion guarantee?
options: The accounts give a true and fair view in all material respects
The business is healthy and able to continue trading normally
Every figure has been checked and is exact to the last dong
No fraud existed in the period, since the auditor reviewed every transaction arising
quiz.explanation: This opinion speaks to the quality of presentation, not to health: a heavily loss-making company still receives one if it presents those losses truthfully. Auditing works on materiality and sampling so it does not cover every transaction, and detecting fraud is not the main objective of a financial statement audit.

quiz.question: The auditor issues a qualified opinion because they could not confirm inventory of 800 billion. What should you do?
options: Discard the whole set of accounts, since anything other than an unqualified opinion voids every figure
See how large that item is against total assets, then reassess the analysis depending on it
Read on as normal, since a qualification is an administrative formality between company and auditor
Wait for next period's interim review, since inventory will be fully confirmed by then
quiz.explanation: A qualification has a limited scope and names the item, so the rest of the accounts remains usable - discarding everything is an overreaction. But it is not a formality: cost of sales, gross margin and turnover all derive from inventory and so all carry that uncertainty. Waiting for the next period does not resolve this period's problem.

quiz.question: How does a "disclaimer of opinion" differ from an "adverse opinion"?
options: A disclaimer is milder than a qualification, while adverse is the most severe of the four
A disclaimer applies to unlisted companies while adverse applies only to public ones
A disclaimer means not enough evidence to conclude; adverse means they concluded the accounts are wrong
A disclaimer is issued at the company's request, while adverse is the auditor's own decision
quiz.explanation: The two differ on whether evidence exists: adverse means the auditor saw enough and concluded the accounts are not true and fair; a disclaimer means they did not see enough to conclude. Both are more serious than a qualification, neither depends on listing status, and a company cannot choose which opinion it receives.

quiz.question: The accounts carry an unqualified opinion with an emphasis paragraph on material uncertainty about going concern. How do you read that?
options: The paragraph is a formality appearing in most reports and carries no notable information
This is a contradiction in the audit report, so the audit firm should be asked to explain it
The emphasis paragraph automatically downgrades the opinion to qualified under current standards
Presented truthfully, and at the same time at risk of not surviving the next twelve months
quiz.explanation: The two are not contradictory: the auditor believes the business has truthfully presented its BAD SITUATION. An emphasis paragraph does not change the type of opinion, and it is not routine - it appears only where there is genuine doubt, which makes it the strongest warning a set of accounts can issue.

quiz.question: Why read the audit opinion before analysing the numbers?
options: Because it decides whether this set of numbers is worth analysing at all
Because the audit opinion already sets out the most important financial ratios, pre-calculated
Because reading in page order is a mandatory requirement of the presentation standards
Because auditors rank companies on a scale so investors can compare them quickly
quiz.explanation: An adverse opinion or a disclaimer leaves every subsequent calculation without a basis, so two minutes of reading first saves an afternoon of analysis. An audit report calculates no ratios, ranks no companies, and no rule requires reading in page order.

practicePrompt.question: The accounts carry a qualified opinion relating to a receivable of 12 billion. Total assets are 6,000 billion and profit after tax is 480 billion. What is the sensible conclusion?
options: The qualification is small against both, so the analysis can continue
Discard this set of numbers entirely, since a qualification means nothing is trustworthy
Deduct the 12 billion straight from profit before starting any analysis
Wait for the next period's review before drawing any conclusion at all
practicePrompt.explanation: A qualification names the item, so the thing to do is measure it: 12 billion is 0.2% of total assets and 2.5% of profit after tax. At that size, even a total write-off would not change the analytical conclusion, so the numbers remain usable. Discarding the whole report is an overreaction and throws away the very advantage a qualification has over a disclaimer - it fences the damage rather than denying everything. Deducting the 12 billion outright is also wrong: the auditor said they could not confirm it, not that it is worth nothing.

application.title: Find the opinion paragraph in two minutes
application.message: Open the audited financial statements of a listed company, find the "Auditor's opinion" section in the opening pages, and identify which of the four kinds it is.
application.secondary: If an emphasis paragraph accompanies it, read that too - it is usually more important than the type of opinion itself.

keyTakeaways: Read the audit opinion before the numbers - two minutes that decide all the analysis behind it
An unqualified opinion speaks to presentation, not to the business being healthy
A qualification names the item; measure how large it is before setting it aside
Going concern doubt is an emphasis paragraph, not a kind of opinion

summary.keyIdea: The audit opinion says whether the numbers are worth analysing, not whether the business is good or bad
summary.commonMistake: Reading an unqualified opinion as a certificate that the business is healthy.
summary.action: Open any company's audit report and find the paragraph stating the type of opinion.
